test_title: PYST 35: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following correctly differentiates between RAM and ROM?

options.text: ROM performs all logical operations, while RAM controls input devices
RAM is permanent memory while ROM is volatile
RAM loses its content when the computer is turned off, while ROM retains its data
ROM is used to store data temporarily during program execution

solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM loses its content when the computer is turned off, while ROM retains its data**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a volatile memory, which means it loses all stored data when the power is turned off.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is non-volatile memory, meaning it retains data even when the computer is powered off.
 
• RAM is used to store data that the CPU needs during program execution, providing fast and temporary access to data.
 
• ROM is used to store firmware or permanent instructions needed for the basic functioning of a computer, such as the system boot process.
 
• RAM is writable and can be overwritten as needed, while ROM is generally read-only or requires special processes to modify.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile Memory:** Memory that requires power to retain stored data. RAM is an example of volatile memory.
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory:** Memory that retains data even when power is turned off. ROM, hard drives, and SSDs are examples of non-volatile memory.
 
• **Firmware:** A type of software permanently stored in ROM or similar non-volatile memory that provides low-level control for a device's hardware.
 
• **Types of RAM:** RAM can be further classified into DRAM (Dynamic RAM) and SRAM (Static RAM). DRAM is slower but cheaper, while SRAM is faster but more expensive.
 
• **EPROM and EEPROM:** Variants of ROM that can be erased and reprogrammed. EPROM uses ultraviolet light for erasure, while EEPROM is electrically erasable.
